extracted.intended_audience: plain TeX users, macro writers, and format designers (people implementing or customizing plain.tex / TeX formats)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and conventions for creating, configuring, and using the plain TeX format (plain.tex): character codes, parameter defaults, register allocation, font family setup, and common macro definitions for typesetting. Useful for macro authors and anyone customizing a TeX format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paragraph structure rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The first paragraph of a new section is not indented. The first paragraph end is recognized by a blank line in the manuscript file; subsequent paragraphs are indented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Control indentation with \parindent; TeX breaks paragraph text into lines (see Knuth & Plass). Example: 'The first paragraph of a new section is not indented... Subsequent paragraphs are indented.*' Ensure files use blank lines to mark paragraph boundaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automatic hyphenation and line breaking
rubrics_metrics.description: TeX hyphenates words automatically when necessary and breaks paragraphs into lines using its line-breaking algorithm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tune line-breaking behavior via parameters like \tolerance, \pretolerance, \hyphenpenalty, \exhyphenpenalty and demerits. Example assignment: \tolerance=500 meaning TeX will tolerate lines whose badness is rated 500 or less.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of primitive control sequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize and use primitives: '\par' (end of paragraph), '\noindent' (begin non-indented paragraph), and '\/' (italic correction).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plain.tex defines many macros on top of these primitives; know which constructs are primitives when designing macros and when relying on core TeX behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parameter assignment to control layout
rubrics_metrics.description: Change parameters (e.g., \tolerance, \looseness, \parindent, \hoffset, \voffset, \baselineskip, \parskip) to alter document formatting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples given: \tolerance=500; \looseness=1; \parindent=4mm; \hoffset=1.5in; \voffset=24pt; \baselineskip=11pt plus .1pt; \parskip=3pt plus1pt minus.5pt. Use these to customize spacing, offsets, and line-breaking tolerance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not modify plain.tex casually
rubrics_metrics.description: The plain.tex file contains preloaded macros and format definitions and should not be modified arbitrarily.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The file itself warns: 'And don't modify the file under any circumstances.' If changes are needed, create a new format (e.g., via INITEX) or build on plain.fmt rather than editing plain.tex directly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish catcode values early
rubrics_metrics.description: A format must establish \catcode values first because commands like \def require characters like '{' and '}' to have the proper category codes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: plain.tex begins by setting \catcode for braces, dollar, ampersand, hash, ^, _, tab, formfeed, etc. Ensure your format sets necessary catcodes before defining macros.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide \dospecials for verbatim copying
rubrics_metrics.description: \dospecials lists characters whose catcodes should probably be changed to 12 (other) when copying things verbatim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use \dospecials when implementing verbatim or copying macros so characters like { } $ & # ^ _ % ~ are handled correctly; Appendix E illustrates usage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use '@' as a temporary letter for private names
rubrics_metrics.description: Temporarily set '\catcode`\@=11' so that '@' behaves like a letter to create private control sequences, then reset it to normal punctuation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This enables private macro names that ordinary users won't normally redefine. Reset with '\catcode`\@=12' when finished.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initialize mathcode table consistently
rubrics_metrics.description: Set up \mathcode table entries consistent with extended character sets and font encodings so math-mode character classifications match available fonts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: plain.tex supplies a large mathcode table and notes INITEX also adjusts digits and letters. Keep mathcodes consistent with the font and character set (see Appendix C and Appendix F).

rubrics_metrics.name: Leave uccode/lccode unless language requires changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Don't change \uccode and \lccode tables unless adapting TeX for languages with more than 26 letters; INITEX already sets reasonable defaults.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hyphenation and \uppercase/\lowercase operations depend on these tables. Modify only in language-specific format packages (see Chapter 8).

rubrics_metrics.name: Set sfcode and provide frenchspacing/nonfrenchspacing
rubrics_metrics.description: Use \sfcode table values to adjust space factor behavior around punctuation; provide macros to switch French spacing behavior.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: plain.tex initializes sfcode mostly to 1000 and defines \frenchspacing (sets punctuation sfcodes to 1000) and \nonfrenchspacing (restores larger sfcodes). Use these to control extra spacing after sentence-ending punctuation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delimiters: don't make braces math delimiters
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not set \delcode for '{' and '}' (leave them -1) because braces are needed for grouping and must not also act as math delimiters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Setting \delcode for braces would break macro argument grouping and lead to 'all sorts of strange things'. Use other delimiters for math-size operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use numeric abbreviations for efficiency
rubrics_metrics.description: Define shorthand numeric control sequences (e.g., \@ne=1, \tw@=2, \@cclv=255) so macros run faster and consume less memory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This convention aids efficiency in macro packages. When documenting macros, you may show long forms for readability but implementations often use these abbreviations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Register allocation ground rules
rubrics_metrics.description:
Rules for register usage so macro packages coexist peacefully: registers 0–9 are for temporary scratch use and may be clobbered; use 
ewcount/
ewdimen/
ewbox/etc. for long-lived allocations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifics: registers numbered 0–9 free but clobbered; \count255, \dimen255, \skip255 are freely available; scratch registers numbered 1,3,5,7,9 should have global assignments; 0,2,4,6,8,255 should be non-\global. Use grouping to restore temporaries and allocate shared registers with \new... macros.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use \allocationnumber abstraction for allocations
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide an abstraction (\allocationnumber) that indicates the most recently allocated register number so macro writers needn't depend on allocation internals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: plain.tex maintains counters and \allocationnumber so packages can query what number was allocated. Do not assume a specific allocation mechanism in higher-level macros.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide \newhelp for memory-efficient help texts
rubrics_metrics.description: Create help texts via \newhelp to store help messages compactly and avoid wasting token memory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: \newhelp\helpout{This is a help message.} followed by \errhelp=\helpout before an \errmessage. This places help text in a control sequence name without taking excess token memory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reserve and protect key constants
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain constants (\maxdimen, \hideskip, \centering, \p@, \z@, \z@skip, \voidb@x) are fundamental and 'must not be changed under any circumstances'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These values are used by format internals and alignment macros; leave them untouched or use as provided by the format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define boolean flags via \newif paradigm
rubrics_metrics.description:
ewif\ifname creates 
ametrue, 
amefalse, and \ifname; the condition starts out false.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this pattern when introducing boolean switches (e.g., \newif\ifalpha creates \alphatrue, \alphafalse, \ifalpha). Implementation detail: \newif initializes the conditional to false.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initialize a comprehensive set of parameter defaults
rubrics_metrics.description: Set sensible defaults for many TeX parameters (line-breaking, penalties, demerits, sizes, tolerances, box/display skips, dimensions, etc.) so the format behaves well out of the box.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: plain.tex example defaults (not exhaustive) include: \pretolerance=100, \tolerance=200, \linepenalty=10, \hyphenpenalty=50, \exhyphenpenalty=50, \binoppenalty=700, \relpenalty=500, \clubpenalty=150, \widowpenalty=150, \displaywidowpenalty=50, \hsize=6.5in, \vsize=8.9in, \parindent=20pt, \parskip=0pt plus1pt, \abovedisplayskip=12pt plus3pt minus9pt, \overfullrule=5pt, etc. Modify these only when you understand their global effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define pseudo-parameters for higher-level spacing
rubrics_metrics.description: Define format-level pseudo-parameters (e.g., \smallskipamount, \medskipamount, \bigskipamount, \normalbaselineskip, \normallineskip, \jot) that behave like TeX parameters but are part of the format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are changed by users like regular parameters. Examples: \smallskipamount=3pt plus1pt minus1pt; \medskipamount=6pt plus2pt minus2pt; \bigskipamount=12pt plus4pt minus4pt; \normalbaselineskip=12pt; \jot=3pt (used for displays).

rubrics_metrics.name: Define font-scaling macros (\magstep)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide macros for common magnification steps to support font scaling (\magstephalf, \magstep#1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: \def\magstephalf{1095} and \def\magstep#1{...} expand to numbers (1000,1200,1440,...). Avoid using assignment operators like \multiply inside expansion contexts that must be expandable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Load and group fonts to form math/text families
rubrics_metrics.description: Load necessary fonts (Computer Modern by default) and group them into families for text and math; preloading commonly used fonts can speed up formats.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: plain.tex defines fonts like \font\tenrm=cmr10 and groups them: \textfont0=\tenrm, \scriptfont0=\sevenrm, \scriptscriptfont0=\fiverm, then defines \def\rm{\fam0 \tenrm}. Preload a minimal standard set (plain.tex aims for 16 basic fonts) and allow local preloads for site-specific needs. Use \preloaded temporarily and \let\preloaded=\undefined at the end to avoid leaving temporary names.

rubrics_metrics.name: Set font hyphen/skew chars where appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Most fonts use default \hyphenchar and \skewchar; math italic and symbol fonts need explicit \skewchar values.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: \skewchar\teni='177, \skewchar\tensy='60. Set these consistent with font metrics so accent placement and italic corrections work properly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide shorthand font switches and math families
rubrics_metrics.description: Define convenient macros like \rm, \it, \bf, \tt, \cal and allocate new math families (\newfam) to support multiple styles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: \def\rm{\fam0 \tenrm}, \newfam\itfam \def\it{\fam\itfam\tenit} and assign \textfont\itfam=\tenit. Also set \scriptfont and \scriptscriptfont for each family.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define frenchspacing and nonfrenchspacing macros
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide macros to toggle sentence spacing behavior by adjusting sfcodes of punctuation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement \frenchspacing to set sfcodes for . ? ! : ; , to 1000 (no extra space after sentences) and \nonfrenchspacing to restore larger sfcodes. Use these macros to match typographic conventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide \normalbaselines abstraction
rubrics_metrics.description: Define a macro (\normalbaselines) that sets \baselineskip, \lineskip, and \lineskiplimit to format defaults for switching type sizes safely.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this macro as the canonical way to restore baseline parameters, facilitating size changes (see Appendix E).

rubrics_metrics.name: Careful implementation of \obeyspaces and \obeylines
rubrics_metrics.description: Define \obeyspaces and \obeylines by changing catcodes to active carefully so partial definitions don't break halfway through.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: \def\obeyspaces{\catcode`\ =\active} with a following global \let to \space; for lines use a grouped definition that ends with '%' to avoid stray spaces. Use \let^^M=\par rather than \def^^M{\par} so constructions like \let\par=\cr \obeylines \halign{...} still work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide \loop...\repeat idiom for iteration
rubrics_metrics.description: Define iterative control-flow macros \loop#1\repeat and supporting \iterate and \next to implement repeatable bodies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implementation uses temporary \next scratch assignment and makes \repeat equivalent to \fi so \loop...\if...\repeat is skippable. Use with care: \loop ... \if... \repeat is a pattern for loops in plain TeX.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define spacing primitives and glue helpers
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide macros for horizontal and vertical spacing such as \enskip, \quad, \qquad, \enspace, \thinspace, \negthinspace, and generic glue helpers \hglue and \vglue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: \def\enskip{\hskip.5em\relax}, \def\quad{\hskip1em\relax}, \def\thinspace{\kern .16667em }. Implement \hglue and \vglue with \afterassignment handlers to allow 'flexible' glue specification: \hglue\skip@=... and restore \spacefactor appropriately inside \hgl@ and \vgl@.

rubrics_metrics.name: Top-of-page glue helpers (\topglue) and interline control
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide \topglue (\nointerlineskip followed by a negative \topskip adjustment) and macros to suppress or restore interline glue (\nointerlineskip, \offinterlineskip).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: \nointerlineskip sets \prevdepth to a large negative so the next box isn't preceded by interline glue; \offinterlineskip sets \baselineskip to -1000pt, \lineskip=0pt, \lineskiplimit=\maxdimen to disable future interline glue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertical spacing macros (small/med/bigskip)
rubrics_metrics.description: Implement \smallskip, \medskip, \bigskip using previously defined pseudo-parameters (\smallskipamount etc).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: E.g., \def\smallskip{\vskip\smallskipamount}. These should be flexible glue amounts (plus/minus) to allow page-breaking behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Penalty and break control macros
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide macros to insert penalties and control break desirability: \break, \nobreak, \allowbreak, tie (~), \slash, and vertical break helpers (\filbreak, \goodbreak, \eject, \supereject).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement \break as \penalty-10000, \nobreak as \penalty10000, tie (~) as \penalty10000\ , slash as '/\penalty\exhyphenpenalty'. Use vertical break helpers with \par and additional glue/penalty logic (\filbreak uses \vfil and negative penalty).

rubrics_metrics.name: Small/med/bigbreak as conditional vertical breaks
rubrics_metrics.description: Define \smallbreak, \medbreak, \bigbreak to insert a break only when the preceding skip is smaller than the corresponding amount.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each does: \par \ifdim\lastskip<\<amount> \removelastskip \penalty-<n> \<skip> \fi. This avoids accumulating excessive vertical space.

rubrics_metrics.name: Box and line-making macros
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide macros to make full-line boxes (\line, \leftline, \rightline, \centerline), zero-width overlays (\llap, \rlap), and an underlining macro (\underbar).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement \line as \hbox to\hsize and variants using \hss; \llap/\rlap use \hbox to 0pt with alignment. \underbar uses math mode to place a rule under its argument; be aware of math/non-math mode usage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define a robust \strut and \strutbox
rubrics_metrics.description: Supply a \strutbox (an hbox with zero width and fixed height/depth) and \strut macro that works in both math and non-math contexts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: \setbox\strutbox=\hbox{\vrule height8.5pt depth3.5pt width0pt} and \def\strut{\relax\ifmmode\copy\strutbox\else\unhcopy\strutbox\fi}. Include a leading \relax to avoid surprises when \strut appears first in an alignment entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use \relax in macros to avoid alignment surprises
rubrics_metrics.description: Insert \relax in macros that may appear at the start of an alignment entry to avoid unpredictable mode behavior.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: \strut and other macros include \relax because TeX is in a somewhat unpredictable state at the beginning of an alignment entry (see Chapter 22).
